Harry Halliday was an English cricketer who was born on July 17, 1855, in West Hartlepool, County Durham. He was a left-handed batsman and a useful right-arm medium bowler. Halliday made his first-class debut for Durham in 1882 and continued to play for the county until 1894.

In his first-class career, Halliday scored 2,376 runs at an average of 15.67, with a high score of 87. He also took 129 wickets at an average of 20.72, with best figures of 7/37. Halliday was known for his aggressive batting style and his ability to hit the ball cleanly.

Halliday also played for North of England XI, Gentlemen of England, and I Zingari during his career. He was a popular and respected figure in the cricketing world, known for his sportsmanship and his dedication to the game.

After his playing career, Halliday remained involved in cricket as a coach and administrator. He passed away on September 4, 1910, at the age of 55. Harry Halliday's contributions to cricket are remembered and celebrated by cricket fans to this day.
